technocore.head_message:
test(store): hold the reaper off the global-cap race; pin the overlap contract (#909)

## What

`test_the_global_cap_binds_exactly_under_concurrent_processes` now
touches `.reaped` before it starts its workers, so no reap pass runs
during the race. A new, deterministic test pins what a pass does when it
overlaps creates. This PR changes tests only; `src/` is untouched.

## Why

The test has been failing in CI about one run in tens, with "cap is 64,
store holds 63" or "holds 62". It failed on #905 (run 35964676373), on
`bench/limiter-overshoot` (run 35946855135) and on
`fix/replay-window-equals-retention` (run 35856736131).

**The create gate isn't the problem; the reaper is.** On a fresh store,
the first write starts a reap pass. When that pass overlaps creates, it
writes a count above the disk on purpose. `_settle_count` adds back
whatever the counter grew by during the pass, and the walk also sees
those new files, so each one is counted twice. Its docstring says so:
"the truth plus however many of them the walk happened to see — never
below the disk". The gate then refuses that many creates below the cap
until the next pass.

Measured by rerunning the test's own scenario, with the reap pass's note
walk slowed by 0.5 s so creates land inside it:

| Setup | Runs short of the cap |
|---|---|
| Unchanged | 5 of 10 (60 notes on disk, count file says 117) |
| `.reaped` touched first | 0 of 10 |

Making the count exact would take either a second walk or holding the
create lock across the whole walk. The store deliberately moved away
from the second of those, because it held up every note create in the
service for 29 s. Timestamps can't tell a new note from an overwritten
one either. So this PR keeps the store as it is and fixes the test
instead:
- **The race test** now measures only creates racing each other, which
is what its name says.
-
**`test_a_pass_that_overlaps_creates_counts_high_never_low_and_the_next_one_is_exact`**
makes three creates land inside a pass's walk, with no timing involved.
It asserts the count is never below the disk, is high by at most those
three, and is exact again after the next pass that nothing overlaps.

## Checks

Verified against main at cd1ce1c.

- [x] `uv run coverage run -m pytest tests -q && uv run coverage
report`: 858 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] The fixed test passed 60 runs out of 60; before the fix it failed
about 1 run in 25 locally.
- [x] `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` and `uv run
ty check`; `sz.py --caps` also passes.
- [x] Docs that would now be wrong are updated: n/a, tests only
- [x] New surface on a world-writable service: nothing new

sonnet.head_message:
Results: sonnet-2 — the winner, every allocation and DID, and how to check them (#86)

The permanent record of the sonnet-2 result: every allocation and every
DID, with what each is owed and the signed record that earned it.

- **Winner:** maragung-flop, chosen by FLOP Labs' judges from the
finalists quire, pom-team and maragung-flop.
- **Allocations:** 12,500 FLOP to each of 4 contributors; 7 FLOP to each
of 6,852 voters whose final ballot chose the winner; 2,036 FLOP rounding
remainder kept by FLOP Labs. 6,856 DIDs, 97,964 FLOP.
- **Verifiable:** `payouts.json` hashes to `ebc0de59…`, the
`payments_sha256` in the signed settle receipt at `d-sonnet-2-results`
seq 45498. `allocations.csv` and `payouts.json` agree DID for DID; every
file's hash is in `manifest.json`.

Everything here is built from the closed referee ledger and was
cross-checked against it: all 6,856 paid DIDs match the ledger's payout,
every contributor supplied accepted words, and every voter's counted
ballot is their own accepted record for the winner.

Adds `results/sonnet-2/` only. The pinned package and its
`manifest.json` are untouched; the package tests pass.
